A BlockDevice/CharacterDevice entry with a crafted path would be rejected at the type check rather than the path check.

summary: Reviewed 1 modified file (TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs). Both changes are security hardening: Ordinal fix closes Tar-Slip bypass on Linux; device-node guard prevents block/char device creation. Guard ordering is correct. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01/A04 (Device-Node Guard — Security Improvement Verified): The new BlockDevice/CharacterDevice/Fifo rejection block (lines 89-93) correctly prevents creation of block/character devices or named pipes on Linux, which could otherwise allow privilege escalation or hardware device access if an attacker controls the archive. Placement is correct: type rejection occurs BEFORE path normalization and the Tar-Slip guard. Entry.Name appears only in the exception message, not in any interpreter. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/ExternalTools/TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs, lines 89-93.

A01 (Tar-Slip Guard — Confirmed Correct): canonicalDest uses Path.GetFullPath + trailing DirectorySeparatorChar (lines 49-51). entryFullPath produced by Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(canonicalDest, normalizedName)) (line 98). Separator normalization at line 97 ensures Unix-style entries (forward slashes) are handled on Windows. StringComparison.Ordinal at line 100 is correct and closes the theoretical Linux bypass. Guard architecture is sound. File: TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs, lines 97-104.

A04 (Pre-existing) — overwrite: true in ExtractToFileAsync (line 112) silently overwrites existing files in the destination. Acceptable for FFmpeg provisioning (re-extraction is idempotent). Would only be a concern if an attacker controls the downloaded archive. File: TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs, line 112.

A09 (Pre-existing, Acknowledged) — No audit logging for extraction events or guard-triggered rejections. The code itself documents this gap in the XML doc comment (lines 16-29) with a detailed TODO specifying LogDebug/LogWarning/LogInformation integration points. No action required until the provisioning-pipeline logging feature is added. File: TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs, lines 16-29.

comments.note: Both changes are correct security hardening. Guard ordering is correct: type guards (symlink, device-node) execute before path normalization and Tar-Slip check, preventing any evaluation of malformed paths for special entry types. Separator normalization (Replace('/', DirectorySeparatorChar)) is pre-existing and correct for cross-platform tar archives. reviewer-applied-fix: Changed 'using var tarReader' to 'await using var tarReader' in ExtractAsync. TarReader implements IAsyncDisposable in .NET 10; using await using is idiomatic for async Infrastructure code per project conventions. With leaveOpen: true the async dispose is a no-op for the underlying stream, so this is strictly non-behavioral. Build verified clean (0 warnings, 0 errors, Release) after the change.
